leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open, and none should be opened. Cash comfortably covers the Gomis bid alone, and the recommended Scheller bid is sized to exactly what remains after it, so the balance lands at zero in every resolution order rather than going negative. The rejected alternative is recorded here because a future run will otherwise rediscover it as a new idea: bidding all three targets is affordable only by going deeply negative when the last bid resolves and then unwinding with two hand-executed sales across the weekend, and it would buy only a marginal gain over the clean swap. A negative balance at matchday start scores zero for the entire matchday, which outranks every other consideration, so that trade is refused.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is shape, not money. Carrying only two attackers leaves exactly one legal formation and forces a non-scorer into the fielded eleven. Tidiam Gomis fixes that as a third attacker and unlocks the stronger shapes; Scheller then compounds the gain by upgrading the weakest defensive slot and pushing the squad's lowest scorer out of the eleven. The remaining gap after that is midfield, which is thin behind Nusa - but midfield is the cheaper problem, and it is explicitly the one being deprioritised this run in favour of the larger points gain. That is the whole content of the Amaimouni-to-Scheller swap.

verdict.headline_short: Execute the swap: remove the standing Amaimouni offer and bid on Tjark
verdict.detail: Execute the swap: remove the standing Amaimouni offer and bid on Tjark Scheller instead, before the Amaimouni offer resolves this morning. This REVERSES the live Amaimouni buy that the last two briefings recommended, and it is said out loud rather than buried. Scheller is the better buy on both axes at once - he adds more than twice as much to the fielded eleven, and he is cheaper at market value. That is not a close call, and previous runs were wrong to keep presenting it as balanced and deferring it. The Tidiam Gomis bid stands untouched and must not be raised unless a rival appears on him. One guard, and only one: if Scheller has drawn a rival bid by the time Georg acts, abandon the swap and leave the Amaimouni offer alone, because the Scheller bid is capped by available cash at a premium below the level at which contested Kickbase listings clear. Act early. The swap is executable from now until the Amaimouni offer resolves, and the last scheduled run before that cutoff leaves well under an hour of runway.

sell.reason: No sale is possible or advisable this run, and that is a structural fact rather than a judgement. At eleven players with exactly one legal formation there are no spare men, so any sale at all drops the squad below a fillable eleven and hands over the hundred-point penalty by Georg's own hand. Bernardo and Widmer both remain designated funding sales and both are frozen until a purchase lands first. Bernardo still carries his knock flag from the opening matchday and is bleeding value daily, which is exactly why he is a sale the moment he becomes legal - but not one hour before.

buy.reason: Scheller is the recommendation, and the standing Amaimouni offer is the thing that has to move out of the way to fund it, because the three bids together exceed available cash and Kickbase will not accept all of them. Scheller is a Paderborn centre-back, listed by Kickbase at exactly market value, still with no rival bid after several hours on the board, and he is the best points-per-euro on the entire board - better even than Tidiam Gomis, who was called the buy of the week two runs ago. Because he is a defender rather than a midfielder he enters the strongest available shape and pushes Widmer out of it, whereas Amaimouni would only displace a zero-scorer from a weaker shape. The bid is capped by cash rather than by judgement: it is exactly what remains once the Gomis bid is covered, and a single euro above it opens a leveraged position. Honest odds, stated plainly: that capped premium sits below the band where contested Kickbase listings clear, so if a rival turns up the bid loses. But three fresh datapoints say the board is quiet - Gosens settled overnight to a single bidder at exactly market value, and both of Georg's own bids have stood unopposed for hours. An unopposed Kickbase bid clears at its own price. Atubolu is the trap of this run and the thing most likely to tempt a future one: a genuinely good, genuinely fit Freiburg keeper listed at exactly market value, whose points barely exceed Baumann's. Only one keeper can ever be fielded, so almost the whole outlay would buy nothing on the pitch, and it is unaffordable in every branch. Avoid.
